title: AI Lessons for Older Students
lede: Ready-to-teach lessons about AI for teenagers. In 40 minutes or less, students take chatbot replies apart, see their own choices turn into training data and work out what to check. Younger teens work with paper, each other and short teacher demos; older students also use the AI tool their school has approved. The whole class pulls it together at the end.

stats.label: Students
stats.value: No accounts at 13–15; the school's AI tool at 16–19

objectives: Explain how a chatbot produces its replies, and why the same question can get different answers.
Recognise the design choices that make a chatbot seem like a friend, and say who gains from them.
Show how past choices used as training data can make an AI system unfair, and suggest what its makers could change.
Weigh clues and evidence about whether a picture, a text or a voice is real, and plan how to check before acting on it.
Map what apps record about them, what they get back, and what they want to change.
Decide when AI helps them learn and when it does the thinking for them, and set their own rules.
Check what a chatbot says against sources, and accept, revise or reject what it writes.
Explain who made a piece of AI-assisted work, when to say AI was used, and who decides the rules for AI at school.

threads.name: What AI is (and isn't)
threads.line: A chatbot produces text from patterns, not from feelings or understanding. Students see how design choices make it seem human.

threads.name: How AI learns
threads.line: Models learn from data that people collect and choose. Students see past choices turn into patterns, and chance shape every reply.

threads.name: When AI is wrong (and how we check)
threads.line: Fluent and confident is not the same as true. Students practise deciding when to trust, when to check and where to look.

threads.name: AI-made content
threads.line: Pictures, texts and voices can be faked. Students weigh evidence by how easily it can be faked, and plan what to do before they act. Older students also ask who made AI-assisted work and when to say that AI was used.

threads.name: Me and AI
threads.line: What apps record about us, what we get back, and the choices we can make about our own data. Older students also look at when AI helps them learn and who sets the rules for AI at school.

bands.line: Lower secondary. Students work in pairs with printed material; AI appears only in short teacher demos.
Upper secondary. Students use the AI tool their school provides, always with a way to do the task without AI.

how_it_works: Every lesson has a teacher page you can read in about ten minutes, and a student PDF to print.
Students work on their own first, then in pairs, and then the whole class pulls it together: individual, pairs, all.
You lead, and the students do most of the work. Suggested wording helps where the words matter, for example to describe what a chatbot does without making it sound like a person.
Every lesson ends with a closing question that each student answers before leaving.
The lessons work on their own or in order. Pick what suits your class.
what_you_need: A printer. The student PDFs are A4 and fit US Letter. Most print well in black and white; when a page needs colour, the teacher page says so.
A board, and a projector for the short teacher demos at 13–15 and for some of the ways to do a step without AI at 16–19.
No devices or accounts for students aged 13–15. In the demos, you use the tool on your own account and students watch.
For ages 16–19: one device per pair, with internet and the AI tool your school has approved.
About ten minutes to read the teacher page, plus the preparation it lists.

gemini-education.min_age: Any age, if the school's administrator switches it on
gemini-education.note: Stricter content rules for under-18 accounts.

copilot-education.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, school account
copilot-education.note: Blocked for students under 13 on school accounts.

claude.name: Claude
claude.note: No exception with a parent's permission. In a school, for teachers only.

snapchat-my-ai.name: Snapchat My AI
snapchat-my-ai.note: My AI is part of the Snapchat app.

ai_use_note: Students aged 13–15 don't need accounts: AI appears only in short teacher demos, on your own account. Students aged 16–19 use the AI tool your school has approved, and every step that uses AI has a way to do it without AI.
reader_note: Readers outside Sweden should verify their own national regulations. AI in education is evolving quickly and country rules differ significantly.
use_rights: For members of the Choosewise community: use these materials with your own students, share them with colleagues at your school, and adapt or translate them for your own teaching. Please don't republish or sell them.
